prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene, which opened the field of moire quantum materials

statement.case_for: I opened with dynamical mean-field theory (B001) first and magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene second, and after reading the eight ballots I move B046 to the top of my configuration. The case is that it is the cleanest prediction-then-discovery chain on the shortlist. Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted in 2011 that flat bands appear at a magic twist angle, and Jarillo-Herrero's group found correlated insulators and superconductivity at that angle in 2018. The result gave a gate-tunable platform for correlated and topological phases, and it has been reproduced and extended across many moire systems by independent laboratories. From a first-principles point of view it is also a case where continuum-model and electronic-structure reasoning anticipated what was measured, which is the kind of theory-experiment closure the committee has repeatedly rewarded. B046 also has the broadest opening support (five top-three placements, two first places), and I treat that as a prompt to re-examine the case, not as merit in itself. The case holds up: the credited trio maps onto the decisive theory and the decisive experiment, which I cannot say of most other entries.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is maturity. The experimental discovery is only about eight years old, the pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is unresolved, and twist-angle disorder and sample dependence still affect many results. Attribution is also incomplete: Yuan Cao as first author, and parallel experimental groups (Dean, Yacoby, Young and others), are outside the credited names, as is earlier twisted-bilayer theory. If the committee judges that a prize should wait until the interpretation settles, B001 is the better-established achievement, with three decades of validation, although its attribution has its own gap in Metzner and Müller-Hartmann.

responses.point: Mehlig ranks B046 only eighth, arguing that it is relatively young, that the superconducting mechanism is not established and that early reproducibility and sample-dependence issues have only partly resolved, so a prize may be better deferred. He also notes for B001 that the work is theory-led and that Metzner's omission leaves an allocation question.
responses.response: I agree on both of the specific caveats and they are the reason B001 remains my first alternative. I disagree that an open pairing mechanism is a reason to wait. The prize would honour the flat-band prediction and the discovery of correlated and superconducting states, not a solved theory of the pairing, and the phenomenology has been reproduced by many groups across several moire materials. Sample variability was largest in the first two years and is much better controlled now. On Metzner, I accept the point and it narrows my enthusiasm for the credited DMFT trio, but I do not think a theory-led achievement is disqualifying when it has this much methodological and quantitative impact.

responses.point: Johansson places B046 third and calls the recognition possibly slightly premature, since the field is about eight years old and the correlated phases are not settled. She ranks the trapped-ion proposal B018 second as a mature and clearly specific discovery.
responses.response: I take the timing concern seriously but I come out differently. Eight years is short, but the field has already produced independent replication, fractional Chern insulators and other moire platforms, so the discovery is secure even where the interpretation is not. I also do not think B018 sets a higher bar for maturity. Its Cirac-Zoller proposal is certainly mature, but the experimental half overlaps with the 2012 control-of-single-quantum-systems prize and leaves Wineland and Monroe outside the credited names, so the attribution is weaker than for B046. I would rank B018 below B046 for that reason, though I would not oppose it as an alternative.

responses.point: Danielsson ranks B046 first because the flat-band prediction and the decisive measurement fit the committee's pattern of a theoretical insight confirmed by experiment, and the field has grown enormously. He still concedes that Cao and other experimentalists are missing from the credit.
responses.response: I share the scientific assessment and find his framing of theory confirmed by measurement convincing. I would add one qualification. The credit problem is real: with three names allowed the trio is the only workable form, but the committee should say in its citation that the discovery was made by the Jarillo-Herrero group and not leave the impression that one person did it. I would not use that omission as a reason to prefer a candidate whose credit is even more diffuse.

responses.point: Kroll ranks the Katori-Ye optical lattice clock (B041) first as a clear, precise measurement with broad reach for tests of constants, geodesy and the redefinition of the second, with a clean two-person credit.
responses.response: B041 is a strong candidate and I agree on the clean attribution and the independent reproduction. My reservation is about novelty of principle: the comb and ion-clock prizes of 2005 and 2012 already honoured the metrological frontier, and lattice clocks are a refinement of that line. B046 opened a new class of materials and a new set of questions, and I weigh that above a further order of magnitude in accuracy. I would not argue against B041 as an alternative if the committee prefers to wait on twisted bilayer graphene.

uncertainties: Whether the committee regards eight years since the experiment as sufficient maturity when the pairing mechanism is still open.
Whether three names can fairly represent the experimental side without Yuan Cao or the parallel groups.
How much weight the committee gives theory-led achievements (B001) against experiment-led ones, given the three-person limit prevents a two-part prize combining B001 and B046.
My recollection of priority details for DMFT (Metzner, Müller-Hartmann) is from memory and cannot be verified from the supplied material.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my provided profile for B046. For B001, my own work uses electronic-structure methods including DFT and dynamical mean-field theory, so I am professionally close to the DMFT community, but my profile documents no personal or institutional tie to Georges, Vollhardt or Kotliar, and I would flag that closeness if the committee turns to B001.
